properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-22: `--shared --graph-path .reflow2/graph` in a folder with no `.reflow2/` serves only reflow2_unavailable: "could not open the server log at .reflow2/graph.server.log: No such file or directory"
properties.source: dev_reflow2 hub session, debug build of main@aef0f0f plus the path fix, while writing tools/test_shared_attach_from_another_folder.py
properties.statement: OBSERVED while writing an end-to-end test: in a fresh temporary folder with no `.reflow2/` directory, a `--shared` client started with `--graph-path .reflow2/graph` was served only `reflow2_unavailable`, with reason, verbatim: "Could not start a shared reflow2 server for this design: could not open the server log at .reflow2/graph.server.log: No such file or directory (os error 2)". No `.reflow2/` was created. With `.reflow2/` pre-created (as tools/reflow2_init.py does), the same command works. NOT AFFECTED: an installed project, since the installer always creates the directory, and a graph path whose parent already exists (test_export_to_reaches_the_daemon uses `<tmp>/graph`). Consequence: `--shared` pointed at a new design location cannot bootstrap it, although plain stdio creates a store "if absent" per the `--graph-path` help text. The error message does name the cause, which is good. Not root-caused. The observed order suggests the daemon log beside the store is opened before any directory is created. Found incidentally; unrelated to the path-spelling fix in progress.
